## GET /v1/images

Operation `image_list`.

`GET /v1/images?scope=<public|silo|tenant|project|user>`, the one image collection. `scope` names which selector is in force and which owner scopes the listing carries:

* `public`: images owned by no scope. The only scope an unauthenticated caller may read, and it takes no selector. * `silo` + `?silo=`: images owned by that silo, and nothing else: no public images, and none merely granted to it. It is an ownership listing, not the silo's view of what it can use, which is the one place this parameter does not parallel `tenant` below. Gated on silo membership; a cross-silo probe sees `404`. * `tenant` + `?tenant=`: every image a member of that tenant can use: public, the tenant's silo's, the tenant's own, and anything granted to that silo or tenant. Gated on tenant membership; a cross-tenant probe sees `404`. * `project` + `?project=`: the `tenant` union plus the project's own images. Gated on membership of the project's owning tenant, which is read from the project rather than taken from the caller. * `user`: the caller's own `User`-owned images. Takes no selector; the owner comes from the credential, so this arm cannot be pointed at another user.

Naming a selector the scope does not use is `400 ScopeNotAccepted`; omitting the one it does is `400 MissingScope`. Neither is ignored.

Paginated per convention 3: `limit` (default 50, capped at 500), `page_token`, and `sort_by`. Only `id_ascending` is accepted, because every keyspace behind this collection is keyed by the image id. The scope and its resolved selector are bound into the cursor, so a token minted for one scope is `400` against another.

| Parameter | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project` | query | no | string (uuid) | Restrict to a single project. |
| `scope` | query | yes | [ImageScopeSelector](schemas.md#imagescopeselector) |  |
| `tenant` | query | no | string (uuid) | Restrict to a single tenant. |
| `limit` | query | no | integer (uint32) | Maximum rows to return. Defaults to 50 and is clamped to 500; zero is rejected rather than treated as "default". |
| `page_token` | query | no | string | Opaque cursor from the previous response's `next_page`. Valid only for the query that produced it. A token replayed against a different selector set or sort order, or modified in any way, is a `400`; it never silently restarts the listing. |
| `sort_by` | query | no | [NameOrIdSortMode](schemas.md#nameoridsortmode) | Order the collection is walked in. Defaults to `id_ascending`. Bound into the cursor, so it cannot change part-way through a walk. |

Responses:

- `200`: successful operation, `application/json`: [ResultsPage_for_Image](schemas.md#resultspage_for_image)
- `4XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
- `5XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)

## POST /v1/images

Operation `image_create`.

Create an image at the owner scope named by `scope` in the body. The server validates `sha256` (64 lowercase hex chars) and `size_bytes` (non-zero) before it touches the store.

Authorization follows the owner: `public` is root-only, `silo` requires membership of that silo, `tenant` / `project` require membership of the owning tenant (for a project, read from the project rather than taken from the caller), and `user` requires that the named user is the caller. A caller outside the named scope sees `404`, never a `403` that would confirm the scope exists.

Returns 409 if the name is already in use within the named scope.

Request body (required): `application/json`: [NewScopedImage](schemas.md#newscopedimage)

Responses:

- `201`: successful creation, `application/json`: [Image](schemas.md#image)
- `4XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
- `5XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)

## PUT /v1/images/{image}

Operation `image_update`.

Edit the mutable metadata (`name` / `description`) on an image. Only those two fields are mutable; the integrity fields (`os`, `version`, `size_bytes`, `sha256`, `id`) are immutable because the id is content-addressed from `sha256` alone (a root import may instead preserve the upstream uuid). Owner (`scope`) is changed by `image_promote`, not here.

Authorization is the same ownership gate as `DELETE /v1/images/{image}`: * `Public` — root only. * `Silo` / `Tenant` / `Project` — any tenant member of the resolved tenant (Phase 0 = same-tenant access). * `User` — only the owning user (or root).

Returns 404 when the image does not exist OR the principal cannot delete it (cross-scope probes never reveal existence), and 409 when a `name` change collides with an existing image in the same scope. The name re-index is a single FDB transaction.

PUT on the image itself rather than POST to a `/metadata` sub-resource: `name` and `description` are fields of the image, not a resource of their own, and there was never anything else at that path to distinguish. Omitting a field leaves it unchanged, which is a PATCH's semantics on a body whose every field is already optional; the wire shape is unchanged.

| Parameter | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | path | yes | string (uuid) |  |

Request body (required): `application/json`: [UpdateImageMetadata](schemas.md#updateimagemetadata)

Responses:

- `200`: successful operation, `application/json`: [Image](schemas.md#image)
- `4XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
- `5XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)

Operation `image_instance_list`.

Blast radius: list the instances whose boot image is this one, trimmed to `{ id, name, state }`. A caller sees only the instances of its own tenant.

Visibility-gated: returns 404 (not an empty list) when the image is not visible to the caller, preserving the cross-scope probe invariant. An empty array means the image is visible but unused.

## PUT /v1/images/{image}/policy

Operation `image_policy_update`.

Replace an image's visibility policy: the whole set of silo and tenant grants (the legacy `acl`), sent and returned wholesale per convention 7. The image `id`, owner (`scope`), and name are untouched; `grants: []` revokes everything.

Wholesale rather than the add/remove pair it replaces, because a delta is only correct against the set the caller last read: two concurrent `revoke`s of different grants used to leave whichever landed second describing a policy its caller never saw. A PUT says what the policy is.

Returns the updated image rather than the policy alone: the grants are a field of the image, so answering with the image keeps a caller's copy correct without a second read.

Authorization is the image-edit ownership gate; a cross-scope caller sees 404. A non-empty policy on a global image is 409: a global image is already visible to everyone, so grants do not apply. Clearing the policy is always accepted.

| Parameter | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | path | yes | string (uuid) |  |

Request body (required): `application/json`: [ImagePolicy](schemas.md#imagepolicy)

Responses:

- `200`: successful operation, `application/json`: [Image](schemas.md#image)
- `4XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
- `5XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)

## POST /v1/images/{image}/promote

Operation `image_promote`.

Change an image's OWNER (`scope`). Visibility is fully determined by the owner: promoting to `global` makes the image visible to everyone and clears any grants; demoting to a silo/tenant scopes it back down. The caller must satisfy the image-edit ownership gate for the CURRENT owner; promoting to `global` or `system` is additionally ROOT ONLY (403 otherwise). A `system`-owned image is operator infrastructure: it never appears in a tenant listing, cannot be booted by a tenant, and carries no grants. The image `id` and content are unchanged. A name collision in the new owner scope is a 409; a cross-scope caller sees 404.

Spelled `promote` for the direction that matters: making an image global is the privileged, fleet-visible move. Demotion travels the same body, because both are one thing, an owner change, and splitting them into two paths would put the same name-collision and scope-authorization logic in both.

| Parameter | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | path | yes | string (uuid) |  |

Request body (required): `application/json`: [SetImageOwner](schemas.md#setimageowner)

Responses:

- `200`: successful operation, `application/json`: [Image](schemas.md#image)
- `4XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
- `5XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
